title: fix(rest,runtime): a sandboxed crash is a fault at the doors mapDataError does not decide
body:
Fixes #17273

Clause-②: no

#15071 converged ONE `/data` door on the ruling that a sandboxed **crash** is a
fault, and wrote the boundary into a pin (`ACCEPTED DIVERGENCE`) rather than
pretending to be done. This closes both faces that pin named, and flips the
spelling with them.

## The two faces, and the count

The card names **exactly two**, counted by its own `###` subsections under
"Two faces still answer a sandboxed crash from the pre-#15071 world" — face 1
`resolveErrorResponse`'s declared-4xx passthrough, face 2 the `/api/v1/actions`
door reading `innerMessage` as intent. Both are converged here, in one delivery.

### Face 1 — `packages/rest/src/error-response.ts`

`resolveErrorResponse` now asks the same `isSandboxCrash` gate #15071 put above
`classifyDataError`'s code-gated arms, before its declared-status passthrough,
and answers **through `mapDataError`** so the two doors are identical by
construction rather than by a second opinion.

Deliberately **not** band-scoped: scoping the gate to 4xx would have converged
the named shape while minting a new divergence one band over (the single door
has answered `500 INTERNAL_ERROR` for a crash declaring a 5xx since #15071, and
the 5xx arm would have kept `503` plus the declared code). The 5xx arm's
unconditional prose-drop is **not** narrowed — the fault terminal withholds
prose too; what moves for that shape is the status and the declared `code`, both
toward the sanitised pair. Pinned as its own case beside the 4xx one.

### Face 2 — `packages/runtime/src/domains/actions.ts`

`unexpectedFault` required `!innerMessage`, reading the presence of that field as
"user code threw this deliberately" — but the runner sets the same field for a
CRASH, to the native error text. So a crash was neither a deliberate throw nor an
unexpected fault, and fell to the 400 terminal carrying `TypeError: …`. A crash
terminal now sits **above** every branch that reads a producer declaration as
intent (including the one that serves `err.status`), and answers the sanitised
500. The crash reading is `isNativeErrorName` from `@objectstack/types` — the ONE
reader `@objectstack/rest` composes into `isScriptFaultMessage`, so the doors
cannot drift.

## Driven, not read — the bytes before and after

The card warned that face 2 was a source reading, never driven. It reproduces.
A body that really crashes inside QuickJS (`return ctx.input.title.trim();` with
a numeric `title`), through the real doors:

Bulk / metadata / UI routes (`handleRouteError`):

```
BEFORE  409 {"error":"hook 'guard' threw: TypeError: ctx.input.title.trim is not a function",
             "code":"DELETE_RESTRICTED","object":"account"}
AFTER   500 {"error":"Internal server error","code":"INTERNAL_ERROR"}
```

`POST /api/v1/actions/:object/:action`:

```
BEFORE  400 {"success":false,"error":{"code":"VALIDATION_ERROR",
             "message":"TypeError: not a function","httpStatus":400}}
AFTER   500 {"success":false,"error":{"code":"INTERNAL_ERROR",
             "message":"Internal server error","httpStatus":500}}
```

…and the same crash carrying a declared `409 DELETE_RESTRICTED` answered `409`
with the `TypeError:` message before, the sanitised 500 now. Note the `BEFORE`
code on the undeclared row: a crash was being reported to clients as
`VALIDATION_ERROR`. That is one step worse than the card predicted, and it is
gone.

The published page was right and the code was wrong: `content/docs/api/error-catalog.mdx`
already states "a `TypeError` / a `ReferenceError` / a driver's own error class
is a crash (500)" for this very route, and this module's own header says
`crash → 500`. **No docs edit is owed** — the code now matches the page.

## The pins, flipped rather than left saying an old thing

- `error-response-structured-arm-door-parity.test.ts` §4 — `ACCEPTED DIVERGENCE
  (#15071 widens it)` → **`CONVERGED (#17273)`**, asserting both doors and the
  whole body. Two cases added beside it: the 5xx band this repair also reaches,
  and a sandboxed-REFUSAL negative control one `innerMessage` away.
- `rest-hook-refusal-message-parity.test.ts` §7 — the `MEASURED AND NOT REPAIRED`
  section is **INVERTED, not deleted**, the discipline §8b in that same file
  already applies: a pin that records a defect is the only thing that would
  notice it coming back.
- `error-response.ts` — the two docblock paragraphs that asserted the divergence
  in prose (the `armSentence` note and the "measured and NOT repaired here"
  paragraph inside the 4xx arm) are corrected in the same edit.

⚠️ The card's third premise — "the parity pin is the only one asserting this
divergence" — is **FALSIFIED**. Four carriers, not one; all four moved. The sweep
was `grep -rn "ACCEPTED DIVERGENCE"` and `grep -rni "not repaired"` over the tree
with control words known present (9 and 30 hits respectively, so a zero would
have been a reading).

## Ablation — the pins fail on the wrong fix

Both crash terminals were removed on disk (mutation proven by `git hash-object`
against the `HEAD` blob, and by anchor occurrence counts falling 1 → 0), the
suites re-run, then restored (`git checkout HEAD -- …`, restoration proven by
blob equality and an empty `git diff HEAD`).

```
ablated  rest    :  3 failed | 78 passed   (409→500, 503→500, 409→500)
ablated  runtime :  3 failed | 17 passed   (400→500, 409→500, 400→500 on the real crash)
restored rest    :  153 passed (3 files)
restored runtime :   20 passed (2 files)
```

Every negative control stayed green in the ablated run — the flip cannot be
green because the surface was deleted.

## Verification

| what | verdict |
|:---|:---|
| `pnpm --filter '@objectstack/rest^...' --filter '@objectstack/runtime^...' build` | exit 0 |
| `pnpm exec turbo run build --filter='./packages/*' --filter='./packages/*/*'` | exit 0, 72/72 |
| `pnpm --filter @objectstack/rest test` | 192 files, **3218 passed**, 1 skipped, 0 failed |
| `pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime test` | 264 files, **3654 passed**, 0 failed |
| `pnpm --filter @objectstack/rest --filter @objectstack/runtime typecheck` | exit 0 (both, source + test layer) |
| `pnpm lint` — repo-wide, `eslint . --no-inline-config` | **exit 0** |
| `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands` → run → `--ran` | **61 derived / 61 run / 0 NOT-MEASURED / 0 UNRUN** |
| `pnpm check:error-status-conformance` | exit 0 — every derivable runtime status documented, every documented status reachable |
| `node scripts/pm/check-clause2-carriers.mjs --pair 18533` | exit 0 — both carriers agree on `no`, **no widening tell in the diff** |

One gate exits non-zero and it is not this PR's: `pnpm check:cross-package-test-inputs`
(exit 1), rooted in `packages/cli/test/init-created-files-summary.e2e.test.ts` —
pre-existing, filed as #18353 / #18348, and it names **zero** paths under
`packages/rest` or `packages/runtime`. Two gates first answered `exit 3`
(`check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `check:type-check-debt` — PREREQUISITE NOT MET,
neither pass nor fail); the full package build above satisfied both and they were
re-run to **exit 0**, which is what the reconciliation counts.

## Docs — swept, nothing falsified, three pages become accurate

The drift check listed `content/docs/protocol/kernel/error-handling.mdx` (via
`resolveErrorResponse`) and `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx` (via
`handleActionsRequest`). Predicate declared before reading: a page is falsified
iff it (a) says a sandboxed crash's own message or the `<kind> '<name>' threw:`
wrapper reaches the caller, (b) documents the declared-status passthrough as
answering a *crashed* body with the producer's status and prose, or (c) prints an
example body / table row this change now renders differently. Merely naming the
symbol, or documenting the sanitised shape #15071 already declared, is not
falsification.

Neither listed page is falsified. `error-handling.mdx` names
`resolveErrorResponse` once, in a sentence about which writer builds the flat
envelope, and its only worked example is a `UNIQUE_VIOLATION` refusal; its
`INTERNAL_ERROR` section already states the 5xx withhold-by-construction rule
this change extends rather than contradicts. `system-context.mdx` matches on an
unrelated sandbox row and says nothing about error status.

The check warns that a page stating a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier
with the emitter, so I swept past the list. Zeros taken with controls:
`grep -rn "threw:" content/docs/` → **0 hits** (control: 144 files mention
`hook`), so no page prints the wrapper anywhere. `content/docs/releases/**` → **0
hits** for the crash rule (control: 14 files mention `action`); nothing there is
falsified and nothing there is touched.

Three pages state the crash rule by its inputs, and all three said **500** while
the code said 400/409 — they were describing the contract this change makes
true, so they go from aspirational to accurate and **no docs edit is owed**:

- `content/docs/api/error-catalog.mdx` — "a `TypeError` / a `ReferenceError` / a
  driver's own error class is a crash (500)";
- `content/docs/ui/actions.mdx` — "**500** — it **crashed**: a `TypeError` in
  your handler … A deliberate `throw new Error('…')` is a 400 rejection";
- `content/docs/api/client-sdk.mdx` — "(400 rejection, 404 / 403 / 503 dispatch
  failures, 500 crash)".

## Scope fences honoured

⛔ No `packages/spec`, no `docs/adr/**`, no `.claude/**`, no `skills/**`, no
`content/docs/releases/`, no `packages/cli/test/commands.test.ts`. No label,
assignee, ready flip, auto-merge arm or enqueue — landing is the PM seat's act.
No new export, no new error code, no new accepted input: the wire loses the
crash text and the producer's code and gains nothing, which is why this is
declared `Clause-②: no`.

⚠️ **The card body predicted `Clause-②: yes`** ("it moves a status a passthrough
decided, on a published door") while the claim comment of record declares `no`
on triage's reasoning (a tightening back to the sanitisation contract #15071
already declared; the leaked surface shrinks). Both readings are on the record
and this PR follows the claim's declaration, which is the machine-read carrier —
flagged here rather than picked silently.

## 维护者速读(草稿)

**改了什么** — 沙箱里的脚本体崩溃(`TypeError` 这类)时,两个已发布的 HTTP 门
本来会把 QuickJS 的调试文本连同一个业务状态码一起发给调用方。现在这两个门都回
标准的 `500 / INTERNAL_ERROR / Internal server error`,崩溃原文只留在服务端日志。

**为什么改** — #15071 已经裁定「崩溃是故障,不是作者声明的那个拒绝」,但只收敛了
一个门,并把边界诚实地写进 pin 再开卡。这张卡就是那两个残余的门;不收敛的话,
同一次崩溃在不同路由上给出两种答案,其中一种把内部异常文本泄露给了 API 调用方。

**风险与代价(含回滚)** — 属于破坏性行为变更:原来拿 4xx / 400 的客户端分支现在
会走 5xx 分支。这正是本次改动的目的(崩溃本来就不是那个业务拒绝)。普通的沙箱
业务拒绝一个字节都没变,已有负向对照测试钉住。回滚 = revert 本 PR 的两个 commit;
无数据迁移、无 schema 变更、无导出变更。

**席位意见** — (留空,由席位定稿)

**你要做的** — 判断「崩溃一律回 500」这个方向是否需要在 5xx band 上也生效(本 PR
认为需要,理由写在代码注释和上面的 Face 1 段);以及确认 `Clause-②: no` 的判定
(卡面正文曾预期 `yes`,分诊与认领判 `no`)。
